Google "Tech companies Off-balance-sheet joint ventures (JVs)" .... are strategic partnerships where two or more companies form a separate legal entity to fund and manage specific projects, allowing the parent companies to keep massive debts off their own financial statements.

Why Keep It "Off-Balance-Sheet"?

Under standard accounting rules (like GAAP or IFRS), if a company owns 50% or less of a joint venture and does not have voting control, it does not have to consolidate the JV’s financial statements into its own.
Instead, the tech company only records its small initial equity investment as a single line item asset. The billions of dollars in debt borrowed by the JV to build the data center remain completely invisible on the tech giant’s primary balance sheet.

The Strategic Benefits for Tech Giants

• Preserving Credit Ratings: Credit rating agencies look closely at debt-to-equity ratios. By keeping data center debt inside a JV, tech companies protect their pristine AAA or AA credit ratings, ensuring their core corporate borrowing remains cheap.
• Capital Efficiency: Building an AI infrastructure network requires hundreds of billions of dollars. JVs allow tech companies to leverage Wall Street's massive capital pools (like private equity and pension funds) rather than draining their own cash reserves.
• Boosting Return on Assets (ROA): Wall Street penalizes companies with asset-heavy balance sheets. By leasing infrastructure rather than owning it, tech firms keep their asset base lean, which artificially inflates efficiency metrics like ROA.

This verse is from the Book of Numbers (Numbers 24:9), spoken by the prophet Balaam as part of his blessings over the Nation of Israel. 
"He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him up? Blessed be every one that blesseth thee, and cursed be every one that curseth thee." (JPS 1917) 
 
Context & Biblical Background 
 
King Balak of Moab hired the prophet Balaam to curse the Israelites as they traveled through the wilderness toward the Promised Land. However, every time Balaam attempted to speak, God compelled him to utter magnificent blessings instead. This specific verse is the climax of his third oracle. 
 
Verse Breakdown & Commentary 
 
• "כָּרַע שָׁכַב כַּאֲרִי וּכְלָבִיא מִי יְקִימֶנּוּ" ("He couched, he lay down as a lion...") 

	• The Imagery: Israel is compared to a powerful lion and lioness 
• The Meaning: When a lion lies down to rest, no animal or hunter dares to disturb or awaken it because they fear its strength. This symbolizes Israel's future security, peace, and formidable power in their land. They will dwell with such confidence that no enemy will dare to provoke them.
• "מְבָרֲכֶיךָ בָרוּךְ וְאֹרְרֶיהָ אָרוּר" ("Blessed be every one that blesseth thee...") 
	• The Meaning: Anyone who brings goodness and blessings upon Israel will be blessed by God, while anyone who curses or harms them will face divine judgment and curses. 
	• The Connection: This phrase directly echoes the original foundational covenant and promise made by God to Abraham in Genesis 12:3 ("And I will bless them that bless thee, and him that curseth thee will I curse"), confirming that the blessings of the Patriarchs apply to the entire nation.
